QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_29

question.text: For an Investment Fund classified as a Category I or Category II AIF, how does TDS apply to income (other than business income) distributed to investors?

answer.text: TDS is deducted at a flat 20% for both resident and non-resident investors
TDS at 10% applies to resident investors and at rates in force to non-resident investors on income other than business income
TDS applies only to foreign investors and not to resident investors
TDS applies to business income distributed to investors but not to any other income

explanation.text: The Logic: For Category I and Category II AIFs treated as Investment Funds, TDS applies to income other than business income payable to investors; the rate is 10% for resident investors and rates in force for non-resident investors. No TDS is required on business income distributed to investors. The Trap: A flat 20% rate, applying TDS only to foreign investors, or applying it to business income all conflict with the Category I/II Investment Fund TDS rule in the source. Note: Source pages 253-255 of Series XIX-A AIF (Category I and II) Distributors workbook.
